title: The Landfall of Devil's Throat
premise: Ines Coldharbour, a desert ranger who has spent twelve years erasing himself from every record, tracks a thief across the salt flats and finds instead a dying prospector clutching a map to the Devil's Throat—a wreck buried in a drowned canyon that holds the sealed ledgers of the Coldharbour family, the dynasty whose crimes made Ines an orphan and whose name he fled. The map is worthless without the tide-tables tattooed on the prospector's skin, and the salvage fleet, led by Ines's cousin Veyra, is six tides behind him and closing. Racing across the nothing, Ines must decide whether the inheritance waiting in the wreck is a fortune, a weapon, or simply proof that he was never invisible at all. In the end he burns the ledgers rather than let anyone—Veyra, the fleet, or himself—wield them, and walks back into the desert carrying only the memory he finally chose to keep.
about_author: Jude Nystrom is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent nine years mapping dry lakebeds before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for landscapes that behave like characters and protagonists who mistake distance for safety.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Tracking a petty thief across the salt flats, Ines reflects on the discipline of his invisible life—no debts, no names, no history—until the trail ends at a prospector's camp instead. The emotional beat is the quiet unease of a man whose carefully measured distance has begun to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The prospector, gut-shot and dying, trades Ines a wax-cloth map of the Devil's Throat for a promise to reach the wreck before the salvage fleet. He dies whispering the name Coldharbour. Ines recognizes his own buried surname and, against every instinct, takes the map. The beat is dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, opening with the thief's brief POV as he sells word of the map to Veyra's salvage fleet. Ines spots their smoke on the horizon and does the arithmetic: six tides. He steals a skiff and a tide-almanac and heads for the drowned canyon. The beat is the first hard turn from flight toward pursuit.

chapters.title: Salt and Skin
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A sandstorm forces Ines to shelter with a salt-gatherer, Maren, who knew the prospector and recognizes Coldharbour workmanship when she sees the map. She reveals the ledgers supposedly record how the family drowned a town to hide their debts. Ines denies it; the denial rings hollow. The beat is memory pressing in from outside.

chapters.title: Veyra
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The salvage fleet's captain interrogates the captured thief and reveals her own stake: she is Ines's cousin, raised on the family name's shame, and she wants the ledgers not for gold but for the power of owning the truth. She burns a village dock for information. The beat is chilling competence—Veyra as the inheritance's other claimant.

chapters.title: The Drowned Canyon
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines reaches the Devil's Throat at dead low tide and dives the first channel, finding the wreck's ribs and a sealed strongroom he cannot open without the tide-tables the prospector tattooed on his own skin—skin now buried a hundred miles back. The beat is the map's cruel joke: the promise requires returning through the fleet.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Ines and Veyra. Ines rides back through fleet territory, trading his ranger's gear piece by piece to stay ahead, while Veyra, reading his trail like scripture, realizes who he is and slows her fleet to let him do the dangerous work. The beat is the horrible intimacy of being hunted by family.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Hold
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Using the recovered tide-tables, Ines opens the strongroom at the fifth tide and finds the ledgers—proof of the drowning, and of his parents' attempt to stop it, erased from every record but this one. He was not abandoned; he was hidden. The beat is grief and fury arriving together.

chapters.title: The Throat Closes
chapters.summary: Ines and Veyra POV. Veyra arrives at the sixth tide and offers Ines partnership: the ledgers would make them untouchable, judges of everyone who ever wronged the name. The tide turns early, the canyon flooding, and Ines chooses—burning the ledgers in the strongroom's air pocket as the water rises, forcing them both to swim or drown. The beat is the climax: renouncing power as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Memory He Kept
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, closing with a short Veyra coda. Ines and a battered Veyra reach shore; the fleet scatters without its prize, and Veyra walks away promising to remember differently. Ines, for the first time in twelve years, writes his own name in a ledger of one—Maren's guest book—and stays a season before moving on, carrying the story instead of the proof. The beat is earned quiet: memory chosen over power.
